p: Tachbrook Park sits on the boundary between Warwick and Leamington Spa, so you get two very different towns for the price of one. Warwick is all medieval streets and timber frames, while Leamington is Regency terraces and wide parades. A bounce session here makes the perfect hinge between the two.

Warwick has plenty of history beyond its castle. The Lord Leycester Hospital, at the top of the High Street, is a wonderfully crooked collection of medieval timber-framed buildings with a pretty garden. St Mary's Church has a tall tower you can sometimes climb for views over the town, and the Market Hall Museum in the Market Place tells the story of Warwickshire.
For a classic photo of the castle, head to St Nicholas Park by the River Avon. There are play areas, open space and riverside paths, and in the warmer months you can often hire boats.

On the canal side of things, the Hatton Locks on the Grand Union Canal are a sight to see, a long flight of locks climbing up the hill just outside Warwick. Watching the narrowboats work through them is surprisingly addictive.
If you're staying longer, Kenilworth Castle is a short drive north, with its dramatic red sandstone ruins, and Stratford-upon-Avon, the birthplace of Shakespeare, is only a little further south-west.

With good links to the M40 and the stations at Warwick and Leamington, this corner of Warwickshire is easy to explore, and there's no shortage of tearooms and pubs to keep the grown-ups smiling between activities.
Do bear in mind that Warwick's town centre is compact and parking near the castle fills up quickly in the school holidays, so arriving early or using the station is a smart move.
